result.title: Autoregressive View Model
result.summary: We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. Through a unified in-context interface, AVM conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions. AVM retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context. We fine-tune a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion transformer with flow matching in an N-in-1-out formulation. We then tune a causal model on its own rollouts to improve photorealism, reduce denoising steps, and limit long-horizon drift. We scale training to approximately 8M scenes and video clips. We evaluate generation capacity and scene persistence across benchmarks for camera control, text control, visual quality, dynamics, sparse and 4D reconstruction, and long-horizon consistency. The results demonstrate that AVM adapts to diverse input and output settings through one in-context interface.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Autoregressive View Model，不建显式三维表示，而以流式视角生成场景：将预训练双向视频扩散 Transformer 以 N 入 1 出方式微调，再用因果模型在自身 rollout 上训练，并从输入与生成历史中检索相关视角组成有界活跃上下文，在约 8M 场景上训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有界活跃上下文」的历史视角检索与长程漂移抑制，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、状态缓存与轨迹训练提供概念类比，但该工作本身面向视角生成而非推理，联系仍需核查。
